name: Catalytic Aerosol Mortar CAM-3 'Lungful'
description: The CAM-3 operates by firing a compressed canister that ruptures at a programmable altitude, releasing a precisely calibrated aerosol suspension of catalytic oxidizing agents. Upon dispersion, a secondary delayed-ignition charge ignites the cloud, producing a deflagration wave tuned to propagate through enclosed spaces with maximum pressure efficiency. The mortar itself is a stubby, break-action single-shot tube with a digital fuse programmer embedded in the grip — operators dial in burst height, dispersion radius, and ignition delay in seconds.
specifications:
weight: 4.1 kg loaded
length: 61 cm
effective range: 40��180 m
blast radius: 8–14 m depending on enclosure geometry
canister capacity: Single shot, break-action reload
fuse delay range: 0.3–6.0 seconds
dispersion modes: Point burst, Wide-area fog, Directional fan
tactical_use: Primarily deployed for building clearance and tunnel engagements where conventional fragmentation is tactically wasteful. Operators fire a round through a doorway or ventilation shaft, letting the cloud settle before detonation — the pressure wave follows corridors and corners in ways solid explosives cannot. Anti-personnel at close range; anti-materiel in confined server rooms or fabrication floors where the overpressure destroys unshielded electronics.
cultural_context: The CAM-3 has a grim reputation in Meridian 88's underground circuits as the weapon of choice for corporate extraction teams conducting 'structural audits' — euphemism for eliminating squatter communities in reclaimed industrial zones. Street gangs fear it disproportionately because it offers no warning and no cover. Owning one marks a person as either deeply connected to military supply chains or deeply dangerous to approach.
known_users: Black-market arms brokers who don't use what they sell
Tunnel-network enforcers in the Undercroft districts
story_hooks: A CAM-3 canister with a tampered fuse is found in a residential block's HVAC system — the ignition timer is set for the building's peak occupancy hour.
A runner is hired to retrieve a stolen shipment of CAM-3 canisters; the job goes sideways when they discover the 'client' is the same extraction team that cleared their old neighborhood.
An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the CAM-3's aerosol formula was field-tested on civilian populations before military sale — and has the atmospheric sensor logs to prove it.
